title: Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act proposes a framework for evaluating how generative artificial intelligence could be used to support or enhance terrorist activities. It calls for the creation of guidelines and oversight mechanisms to identify, monitor, and mitigate such risks while balancing innovation and security.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 establishes rules for measuring and reducing the environmental footprint of AI systems, from energy consumption to electronic waste. It requires companies to report impacts, adopt greener practices, and offers incentives for developing low‑impact AI solutions.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 aims to keep human doctors as the primary decision-makers in healthcare, limiting the use of artificial intelligence in diagnosing and treating patients. It sets strict rules and oversight to ensure AI tools can only assist, not replace, professional medical judgment.

title: Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 37 - 7.
summary: The Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act is designed to increase the export of AI technologies, including both hardware and software, by providing incentives and support for U.S. companies. It aims to enhance global competitiveness while ensuring compliance with national security and trade regulations.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Forwarded by Subcommittee to Full Committee by Voice Vote.
summary: The Open-Source AI Leadership Act is designed to encourage the development and collaboration of AI technologies through open-source initiatives, positioning the country as a global leader in AI innovation. It promotes investment, research, and partnerships that prioritize transparent, community-driven AI solutions.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 seeks to make sure that any AI systems used by the Department of Veterans Affairs are built and used in a way that respects veterans’ privacy, safety, and rights. It sets up rules, oversight, and accountability so that veterans can trust the technology they receive.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act aims to strengthen the protection of advanced artificial intelligence systems by setting strict security standards and oversight. It requires developers to implement robust safeguards, conduct risk assessments, and report incidents to regulators to ensure AI technologies are safe and reliable.

title: Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: The Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026 aims to reduce bias in AI and other algorithm-driven decisions. It proposes new regulations and oversight to ensure fairness in data, model training, and deployment of algorithmic systems.

title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 establishes legal frameworks to protect AI models from theft, including penalties for unauthorized copying and distribution. It also encourages developers to adopt stronger security measures and best practices to safeguard their intellectual property.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 is designed to hold companies that use automated decision‑making tools responsible for how those tools affect people’s lives. It requires firms to assess and publicly disclose the fairness, accuracy, and potential biases of their algorithms, especially when those systems influence significant outcomes such as credit, employment, or housing.

title: Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act requires defense agencies to rigorously test and validate AI systems before deployment, ensuring they function safely and as intended. It also mandates regular reporting on AI performance and any adverse events to maintain accountability and continuous improvement.

title: LIFT AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The LIFT AI Act is proposed legislation aimed at promoting safe and responsible AI development. It seeks to establish standards for transparency, accountability, and risk mitigation in AI systems.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act would require companies using AI in China to disclose the energy usage and environmental impact of their systems, helping regulators monitor and manage the sector’s carbon footprint. It also sets standards for AI safety, data security, and operational transparency, aiming to protect public safety and national security.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is a law designed to safeguard democratic elections from the misuse of AI technologies that could spread misinformation or manipulate voters. It aims to set guidelines and oversight for AI-generated content used in political campaigning, ensuring transparency and accountability to preserve the integrity of the electoral process.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act is a proposed law that would set up oversight for AI systems capable of learning and changing their own behavior. It aims to keep these systems safe and transparent by requiring regular monitoring, reporting, and risk assessments.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act establishes a temporary pause on the construction and operation of new AI data centers. This measure aims to address concerns about environmental impact, energy consumption, and data privacy while the government evaluates long‑term regulations.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act seeks to limit the energy consumption of AI data centers so that families are not burdened with higher electric bills. It proposes measures such as energy‑efficiency standards and possible subsidies to keep household energy costs affordable.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary halt on building new data centers dedicated to AI workloads. This pause aims to curb rapid expansion, reduce environmental and energy‑consumption impacts, and give policymakers time to develop comprehensive regulations for AI infrastructure.

title: LIFT AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 34 - 1.
summary: The LIFT AI Act is a proposed law aimed at regulating artificial intelligence to make sure it is safe, transparent, and accountable. It seeks to set clear guidelines for developers and users so that AI can be used responsibly while still encouraging innovation.

title: Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026 establishes guidelines to ensure AI‑powered toys for children are safe and secure. It requires manufacturers to meet testing standards, provide clear usage instructions, and implement safeguards against harmful content and data misuse.

title: Youth AI Privacy Act
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Youth AI Privacy Act is a proposed law aimed at protecting minors' privacy when interacting with artificial intelligence technologies. It establishes strict rules for data collection, use, and sharing by AI systems that engage with children, requiring transparency and parental consent to prevent exploitation.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act mandates a comprehensive report on the state of artificial intelligence development and deployment in China. It requires regular updates to the government and public to ensure transparency and alignment with national goals.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act establishes rules to guide how AI models are developed, tested, and put into use, making sure they are safe, fair, and clear about how they work. It requires companies to track and report on their models, give people a way to understand and challenge decisions, and follow strict standards for privacy, security, and accountability.

title: A bill to provide for the delivery of artificial intelligence functional bills of materials, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The bill establishes a framework for creating and distributing functional bills of materials (FBOMs) for artificial intelligence systems, promoting transparency, accountability, and security in AI development. It also includes additional provisions for oversight, compliance, and risk management related to the deployment of AI technologies.

title: Workforce for AI Trust Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Workforce for AI Trust Act is proposed to build a skilled and diverse AI workforce that can develop trustworthy AI systems. It would fund education, training, and research programs to ensure that experts are ready to create and oversee AI responsibly and ethically.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This act seeks to stop companies from charging excessive prices for AI services and from manipulating wages in AI-driven labor markets. It establishes regulations and penalties to ensure fair pricing and protect workers’ wages in the AI economy.

title: FARM AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Agriculture.
summary: The FARM AI Act of 2026 establishes rules for how artificial intelligence can be used in agriculture, ensuring that AI tools in farming are safe, transparent, and respect data privacy. It also encourages the adoption of AI to boost crop yields and sustainability while reducing environmental harm.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 619.
summary: This act encourages the use of artificial intelligence in banking, insurance, and other financial sectors by creating a supportive regulatory framework and providing funding for research and development. It also sets out safeguards to protect consumers, maintain transparency, and prevent unfair or risky practices.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
summary: The Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act seeks to accelerate the adoption of artificial intelligence within banking and finance by easing regulatory barriers and encouraging collaboration between industry and regulators. At the same time, it establishes guidelines to protect consumers, ensure data security, and prevent misuse of AI‑driven financial tools.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act aims to support the development and retention of skilled professionals in artificial intelligence and related fields. By providing incentives, training programs, and funding opportunities, the act seeks to foster innovation and maintain national competitiveness in AI technology.

title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
summary: The “No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act” is a law that bans the establishment or operation of artificial‑intelligence data centers on land owned or managed by the federal government. It aims to protect federal property, reduce environmental impact, and prevent security risks associated with large AI infrastructure on public land.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K‑12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 seeks to embed artificial‑intelligence education into all U.S. elementary, middle, and high‑school curricula so that students gain a basic grasp of how AI works and the ethical questions it raises. The law also requires schools to provide professional development for teachers, supply necessary resources, and establish evaluation methods to measure AI readiness across districts.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 aims to equip students and teachers with the knowledge and skills needed to understand and responsibly use artificial intelligence. It sets out guidelines for incorporating AI education into school curricula, provides resources for professional development, and establishes standards for evaluating AI literacy in students.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 sets out regulations to ensure artificial intelligence is safe and ethical, covering transparency, accountability, and risk mitigation. It also outlines penalties for non‑compliance and encourages responsible AI development.

title: Understanding AI in the Classroom Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Understanding AI in the Classroom Act is a proposed law that aims to clarify how artificial intelligence tools can be integrated into educational settings. It outlines guidelines for teachers, students, and administrators to ensure responsible and effective use of AI while protecting privacy and fostering learning.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that every American and community impacted by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center should have the right to transparency and local autonomy.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives says that anyone in the United States, especially people who live near an artificial‑intelligence data center, must have the right to know what is happening and to make local decisions about the site. This policy emphasizes transparency and local control for communities affected by the building or running of AI data centers.
